rv.q: Back then, the play was an appetizer for Beckett’s meatier Endgame. Now it’s the main event, generously but weirdly paired with its own curtain raiser: Godot’s To-Do List, a comic spoof of Beckett’s most famous work by young writer Leo Simpe-Asante.
If this is a slightly scrappy drama, it bewitches with hope, romance and heart.
In short – though this may not be among the most heartbreaking of Krapps – all the skill and presence you’d expect from Oldman is very much in evidence; bleakly absorbing.
His performance in Krapp … a fun and quirky opener
The play’s ending is a perfect balance of joy and gloom, all marvelously managed in a great production.
The script feels slightly unfocused, prone to overreaching.

cn.t: Akhtar's heartfelt two-hander tackles homophobic persecution and asylum issues through a charming love story, but critics find the 80-minute runtime leaves important themes underexplored and the script somewhat unfocused.
